title: Bernie Sanders Says We Should Only Work 4 Days A Week. Working Families Should Benefit From The AI Boom, Not Just Billionaires
key_facts: Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Representative Mark Takano (D-CA) reintroduced the Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act in September.
The bill would lower the standard workweek from 40 hours to 32 over four years with no loss in pay or benefits, and lower the overtime threshold to 32 hours.
Sanders said AI and robotics will radically transform the economy and the financial gains should benefit working families, not just billionaires and corporate CEOs.
Sanders wrote that nearly $80 trillion in wealth has been redistributed from the bottom 90 percent to the top 1% over the last 50 years.
Takano said the 40-hour week was set in law nearly 90 years ago, before smartphones, the internet and AI.
Sanders made a similar argument in a 2024 Senate proposal.
The article contrasts this with Elon Musk's 2025 prediction that working will be optional in less than 20 years.
quote_evidence: The pair reintroduced the Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act in September.
The legislation would gradually lower the standard workweek from 40 hours to 32 over four years while keeping weekly pay and benefits intact.

"At a time when artificial intelligence and robotics will radically transform our economy, it is imperative that the financial gains from this new technology benefit working families, not just a handful of billionaires and corporate CEOs," Sanders said in a statement announcing the legislation.
why_it_matters_hint: A long-running labour proposal is being tied to AI gains, but it is a bill reintroduced in September and not law.
event_date: Sep 2026 (bill reintroduced; the exact day is not stated)
